marta (support): FinEdge escalated — intermittent 429s during a batch embedding job. Window ~2026-03-15T14:02:00Z -> 2026-03-15T14:12:00Z. They say bursts every ~30s for ~2m. They attached one response body and headers. Asking for repro artifacts to hand to SRE.
liam (sre): got it. Can you paste the raw response headers & a sample request-id from the 429s? Also need the client-side concurrency and whether they use a single API key or multiple keys.
marta (support): pasted what customer sent — see below (redacted):

Response (from customer):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-quota-limit: 600
x-rw-quota-remaining: 0
x-rw-quota-window: 60
x-rw-request-id: req-fin-20260315-9f2c
content-type: application/json

Body:
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded", "type":"quota_error"}}

They said they were sending 20 concurrent streams of 8-10 tokens per request (embeddings batch), single API key.
nikita (infra): thanks. Two immediate asks for FinEdge to reproduce and for us to validate: 1) capture a HAR or curl trace that includes the response headers and the x-rw-request-id, 2) run a small repro that simulates their concurrency so we can compare token counts vs quota windows. Provide them this exact curl + small loop (replace $KEY):

```bash
# single request with explicit X-Request-ID
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
     -H "X-Request-ID: req-fin-REPRO-1" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"input":["one","two","three"],"model":"text-embedding-ada-001"}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

# quick concurrency test (bash, 10 parallel)
for i in $(seq 1 10); do \
  XID=req-fin-par-$i; \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Request-ID: $XID" -d '{"input":["a"],"model":"text-embedding-ada-001"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &\
 done; wait
```

Ask them to run that while we monitor and to paste back the `X-Request-ID` values for any 429 responses.
liam (sre): also ask them to capture response headers for successful requests around the spike. The pattern I want: x-rw-quota-remaining and a per-minute window header. If they can show a timeline with request-ids and headers we can correlate to our internal rate-limiter logs. If they can’t run HAR, ask for a debug-bundle from their host: run `rw-support collect --req-ids req-fin-REPRO-* --out finedge-debug.tar` and upload link to support portal.
marta (support): customer sent back a short timeline (they anonymized):
- 2026-03-15T14:03:18Z req-fin-20260315-9f2c -> 429 (x-rw-quota-remaining: 0)
- 2026-03-15T14:03:21Z req-fin-20260315-9f2d -> 200 (x-rw-quota-remaining: 12)
- 2026-03-15T14:03:44Z req-fin-20260315-9f3a -> 429 (x-rw-quota-remaining: 0)
- 2026-03-15T14:04:10Z req-fin-20260315-9f4e -> 200 (x-rw-quota-remaining: 580)

They also said they rotate keys every 5 minutes (one active key at a time) but all from same IP range.
liam (sre): pattern looks like a per-key short window plus global smoothing. Two hypotheses: 1) their client batches aggressively and the token accounting pushes some requests over the per-minute bucket causing bursts of 429s, 2) we had a short enforcement change in that region — I'll check rate-limiter logs for those req ids. Can you get them to run the concurrency script but include `-D headers.txt` to save headers from curl so they can paste exact x-rw-* values?
marta (support): forwarded instructions. Also asked them to run `curl -I` on a known-good endpoint to check for any proxy caching removing headers.
nikita (infra): started a correlation search on our side for request ids: `req-fin-20260315-9f2c`, `req-fin-20260315-9f3a`, `req-fin-20260315-9f4e` — grabbing rate-limiter traces and the token accounting timeline. If we see server-side enqueue/drop events we'll post here. ETA ~15m.
deploy-bot: [automated] rate-limiter-config-change: region-us-west-2 updated quota-window from 60 -> 30s at 2026-03-15T14:03:30Z by config-rollout (id: cfg-789). :warning:
liam (sre): aha — that rollout coincides exactly with the customer's window. That would change effective window mid-run and could cause the observed 429s during the transition. Nikita — will that produce transient 0 remaining headers? If so, note that the x-rw-quota-window header may reflect the new window after the rollout.
nikita (infra): yes, a rollout like that can make in-flight counters hit zero for a short period while we reconcile. I'm pulling per-instance traces to show enforcement duration.
marta (support): told customer: 1) collect HAR/curl traces and the X-Request-IDs for failures, 2) run the concurrency script, 3) upload debug bundle if possible. I also apologized and offered a one-time credit pending root cause. They said they'll run tests and reply within the hour. :thumbsup:
liam (sre): thanks — once they post the request-ids we can map to the rollout timeline and confirm. If rollout is the root cause we'll annotate the incident and follow up with a postmortem note for config rollout safeguards.
nikita (infra): adding internal action item: add rollout-to-rl enforcement grace (TICKET-5623). Will update here when traces are ready.
marta (support): closing loop for now, will re-open thread when customer uploads artifacts. :eyes:
